module_title: Introduction to Essential Oils for African Small Business

lessons.title: What Are Essential Oils? A Simple Explanation for Beginners
lessons.body: Essential oils are concentrated plant extracts. Think of them as the 'lifeblood' of a plant: they carry the plant's scent and protect it from pests and disease. When you crush a lemongrass leaf, you smell that sharp lemon aromaâthat's the essential oil. To get the oil out, we use methods like steam distillation. In Africa, you can build a simple still using a pot, a lid, and a copper pipe. For example, 10 kg of fresh lemongrass yields about 30-50 ml of oil. That's roughly 1,000-1,700 drops. The oil is very strong: one drop of eucalyptus oil equals about 20 cups of eucalyptus tea in terms of active compounds. That's why we dilute them. Essential oils are not 'oily' like cooking oil; they evaporate quickly and don't leave a grease stain. They dissolve in alcohol or carrier oils like coconut or jojoba. You'll store them in dark glass bottles with a dropper cap. A 10 ml bottle holds about 200 drops. In Africa, you can find these bottles at packaging shops in Nairobi, Lagos, or Accra for $0.30-$0.50 each. Always label with the plant name, date, and batch number. Never use essential oils undiluted on skin, except for tiny spot treatments like tea tree on a pimple. Start with a 2% dilution: 12 drops per 30 ml of carrier oil. That's safe for most adults. Essential oils are powerful, so respect them. This module will show you how to make, use, and sell them profitably.

lessons.title: Why Lemongrass, Eucalyptus, and Tea Tree Are Perfect for African Markets
lessons.body: Lemongrass, eucalyptus, and tea tree grow well in many African climates, which keeps your costs low. Lemongrass (Cymbopogon citratus) thrives in warm, rainy areas from Ghana to Kenya. You can harvest it 3-4 times a year. A 10 m x 10 m plot can yield 200-300 kg of fresh leaves per harvest. That's enough to produce 600-1,500 ml of oil. Eucalyptus (Eucalyptus globulus) grows fast in highland regions like Ethiopia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe. A mature tree can give 50-100 kg of leaves per year. Tea tree (Melaleuca alternifolia) prefers subtropical areas like parts of Malawi and Mozambique, but it can be grown in pots or greenhouses. These three oils have strong local demand. In African homes, lemongrass is used for fever and malaria symptoms; eucalyptus for coughs and colds; tea tree for skin infections and wounds. Clinics and traditional healers buy them. You can sell a 10 ml bottle for $2-$5 in local markets or $8-$15 online. Production cost per 10 ml is about $0.50-$1.00. That's a 300-500% profit margin. Plus, you can sell the leftover plant material as compost or animal feed. The global market for these oils is growing, but you don't need to export to make money. Start by selling to neighbours, pharmacies, and salons. With minimal capitalâ$50 for a small still and $20 for bottlesâyou can start. The demand is there; you just need to supply consistently.

lessons.title: Local Uses of These Oils in African Homes and Clinics
lessons.body: In many African homes, lemongrass oil is a first aid staple. For fever, mix 2 drops of lemongrass oil with 1 tablespoon of coconut oil and rub on the chest and back. For mosquito repellent, combine 10 drops of lemongrass oil with 30 ml of carrier oil and apply to exposed skin. In clinics, nurses use eucalyptus oil in steam inhalation for respiratory infections. Add 3 drops to a bowl of hot water, cover your head with a towel, and breathe for 5 minutes. Tea tree oil is used for fungal infections like athlete's foot: mix 5 drops with 10 ml of coconut oil and apply twice daily. For minor cuts, clean with water, then apply 1 drop of tea tree oil directly. Traditional healers often use these oils in massage blends for joint pain. A common recipe: 10 drops eucalyptus, 5 drops lemongrass, 30 ml baobab oil. Massage into sore muscles. In clinics, midwives use tea tree oil to sanitise surfaces: add 20 drops to 500 ml of water in a spray bottle. Always label your blends and note the date. For children under 6, use half the adult dilution. Pregnant women should avoid eucalyptus and lemongrass unless advised by a doctor. These oils are not a replacement for medical care, but they are powerful allies. You can package them as 'African home remedies' for tourists and locals. Sell a 'Fever Relief' roll-on (10 ml) for $3. A 'Cough & Cold' inhaler stick for $2. The market is ready.

lessons.title: How to Start a Small Essential Oil Business with Minimal Capital
lessons.body: You can start an essential oil business with as little as $100. Here's a step-by-step plan. First, source raw materials. If you don't grow your own, buy fresh lemongrass from local farmers at $0.50 per kg. Eucalyptus leaves are often free if you ask tree owners. Tea tree is harder; start with lemongrass and eucalyptus. Second, build or buy a still. A 20-litre stainless steel pot still costs $50-$80 online or from a local welder. You'll also need a heat source (gas or firewood), a condenser (copper coil), and collection bottles. Third, produce your first batch. Steam distillation: fill the pot with chopped leaves and water, boil, and collect the oil. A 20-litre still yields 10-20 ml of oil per batch. Do 10 batches to get 100-200 ml. Fourth, packaging. Buy 10 ml amber glass bottles with dropper caps at $0.30 each. Print labels at a local shop for $0.10 each. Fifth, pricing. Sell wholesale to shops at $1.50 per bottle, retail at $3-$5. Sixth, marketing. Use WhatsApp, Facebook Marketplace, and local markets. Offer free samples to clinics and salons. Keep records: track your costs and sales. Reinvest 50% of profits into more bottles and raw materials. Within 3 months, you can have a steady income. Don't quit your day job yetâstart part-time. Join a local business group for support. The key is consistency and quality. Always test your oil for purity: a drop on paper should evaporate without leaving a grease spot.

lessons.title: Legal Requirements for Selling Essential Oils in Your Country
lessons.body: Before you sell essential oils, you must follow local laws. In most African countries, you need a business permit. In Kenya, register with the Registrar of Companies for a sole proprietorship (about $20). In Nigeria, register with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) for a business name (about $10). In Ghana, register with the Registrar General's Department. You also need a tax identification number (TIN). For health and safety, essential oils are often classified as cosmetics or traditional medicines. In South Africa, you must comply with the Medicines and Related Substances Act if you make medical claims. In Kenya, the Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) may require product testing. For cosmetics, you need a licence from the Pharmacy and Poisons Board. In Nigeria, NAFDAC regulates food and drugs; for cosmetics, you need NAFDAC registration. This can cost $100-$500 and take 2-6 months. To avoid trouble, don't make medical claims like 'cures malaria.' Instead, say 'traditionally used for.' Label your products with ingredients, batch number, and expiry date. If you sell online, you may need an e-commerce permit. For exports, you need phytosanitary certificates and comply with destination country rules. Start small: sell to friends and local shops without formal registration until you validate demand. But once you scale, get legal. Join a local essential oil association for guidance. Hire a lawyer if needed. The cost of compliance is worth it to avoid fines or closure.

lessons.title: Setting Up Your First Essential Oil Workspace at Home
lessons.body: You don't need a factory. A small, clean corner of your home can work. Choose a room with good ventilationâessential oil vapours can be strong. You need a sturdy table, a heat source (gas cooker or hot plate), and a water source. For distillation, set up your still near a window or under a shade. Keep a fire extinguisher nearby. Organise your workspace into three zones: raw materials, production, and packaging. Store fresh leaves in baskets or sacks, away from direct sun. Keep your still on a stable surface. Use a thermometer to monitor temperature: steam distillation works best at 100Â°C. Collect oil in a dark glass bottle placed in a bowl of cold water. After distillation, let the oil separate from water (hydrosol) for 30 minutes. Use a separatory funnel or a syringe to collect the oil. For packaging, have a clean table with bottles, labels, and a small funnel. Wear gloves and an apron. Keep a notebook to record batch numbers, dates, and yields. Safety: never leave the still unattended. Keep children and pets away. Store essential oils in a cool, dark cabinet. Label everything. A basic setup costs $100-$150: still ($80), bottles ($20), labels ($10), thermometer ($5), and gloves ($5). You can start on a balcony or in a shed. If you rent, check your lease. In many African cities, home-based businesses are allowed if they don't disturb neighbours. Start small, keep it clean, and you'll be ready to produce.

quiz.q: What is the primary method used to extract essential oils from plants like lemongrass?
quiz.explanation: Steam distillation is the most common and affordable method for extracting essential oils from leaves and grasses.

quiz.q: How many drops are roughly in a 10 ml bottle of essential oil?
quiz.explanation: A 10 ml bottle typically contains about 200 drops, as 1 ml is approximately 20 drops.

quiz.q: What is a safe dilution for essential oils for most adults?
quiz.explanation: A 2% dilution (12 drops per 30 ml carrier oil) is generally safe for adults.

quiz.q: Which of these oils is known for its use in treating skin infections?
quiz.explanation: Tea tree oil has strong antimicrobial properties and is commonly used for skin infections.

quiz.q: What is the approximate yield of essential oil from 10 kg of fresh lemongrass?
quiz.explanation: 10 kg of fresh lemongrass typically yields 30-50 ml of essential oil.

quiz.q: Which African region is best suited for growing eucalyptus?
quiz.explanation: Eucalyptus grows well in highland regions like Ethiopia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe.

quiz.q: What is a common local use of lemongrass oil in African homes?
quiz.explanation: Lemongrass oil is traditionally used to reduce fever by rubbing diluted oil on the chest and back.

quiz.q: How many drops of eucalyptus oil are typically added to hot water for steam inhalation?
quiz.explanation: 3-5 drops of eucalyptus oil in hot water is a standard steam inhalation recipe.

quiz.q: What is the recommended dilution for tea tree oil for athlete's foot?
options: A) 1 drop in 10 ml carrier oil
B) 5 drops in 10 ml carrier oil
C) 10 drops in 10 ml carrier oil
quiz.explanation: 5 drops of tea tree oil in 10 ml of carrier oil is a safe and effective dilution for fungal infections.

quiz.q: Which group should avoid using eucalyptus and lemongrass oils?
quiz.explanation: Pregnant women should avoid eucalyptus and lemongrass oils unless advised by a doctor.

quiz.q: What is a simple recipe for a muscle pain massage blend?
options: A) 10 drops eucalyptus, 5 drops lemongrass, 30 ml baobab oil
B) 5 drops tea tree, 5 drops lavender, 30 ml coconut oil
C) 10 drops lemongrass, 10 drops eucalyptus, 10 ml water
D) 20 drops tea tree, 30 ml olive oil
quiz.explanation: This blend combines eucalyptus and lemongrass in a carrier oil for muscle pain.

quiz.q: What is the approximate cost of production per 10 ml bottle of essential oil?

quiz.q: At what temperature does steam distillation typically work best?
quiz.explanation: Steam distillation works best at around 100Â°C, the boiling point of water.
